newsitem.title: POLAND: Bulgaria seeks equal start on European integration.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria seeks equal start on European integration.

text.p: Bulgarian President Petar Stoyanov said on Wednesday that he and his Polish counterpart had agreed that all former communist countries should start talks on joining Western structures at the same time.

Stoyanov, on a five-day trip to Warsaw, Prague and Budapest reaffirming Bulgaria's desire to join Western European structures such as the European Union and NATO, said he wanted his visit to be a catalyst for good regional cooperation.

"In talks with President (Aleksander) Kwasniewski, he backed my views that all former socialist states should begin negotiations about full entry to these organisations at the same time," Stoyanov told a news conference in Warsaw.
He said however that some countries would enter Western European structures before others and this should not create envy between the former Soviet bloc states.

Kwasniewski said he had backed Bulgaria's bid to enter the Central European Free Trade Agreement (CEFTA) and offered cooperation in building electrical power plants, galvanisation plants as well as transforming its agriculture sector.
Stoyanov said Bulgaria would use Poland's example of how to transform its economy and hoped for improved ties between the countries in foreign trade, tourism and culture.
"For Bulgaria it is very important to learn both from Poland's successes and its failures on the road to the EU and NATO," Stoyanov said.
"Poland is one of the leaders in this respect," he added after the meeting with Kwasniewski.
Stoyanov took office on January 22, inheriting a severe economic and political crisis. Bulgaria has fallen far behind other East European states considered its economic equals in the early 1990s.
Stoyanov will visit the Czech Republic on February 28 to March 1, then Hungary on March 1 to 2.
